tools.name: check_eol
tools.description: Check whether a specific version of a software product is end-of-life (EOL). Returns lifecycle status, the EOL date, days remaining or days past EOL, and the latest release. Use this for "is X version Y still supported?" questions.

tools.name: get_risk_score
tools.description: Get the proprietary EOL Risk Score™ (0–100) for a product version, with the four-factor breakdown (EOL recency, attack surface, CISA KEV exposure, extended support). Omit "version" to score the product's highest-risk (most recently end-of-lifed) release. Use this to quantify how dangerous it is to k

tools.name: scan_stack
tools.description: Audit a whole stack at once. Provide a list of products (optionally with versions) — e.g. parsed from a package.json, Dockerfile, or SBOM — and get an EOL Risk Score for each, so you can see what is unsupported and dangerous in one call. Free tier: up to 5 items; Pro: up to 50.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List or search the products endoflife.ai tracks (459+). Pass an optional "query" substring to find the canonical slug for a product before calling the other tools (e.g. "postgres" → "postgresql"). Returns matching product slugs.

tools.name: get_product_lifecycle
tools.description: Get the full version history for one product: every tracked version/cycle with its release date, EOL date, support status, and EOL Risk Score™. Use for "give me the whole EOL schedule for X".

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_products" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List or search the products endoflife.ai tracks (459+). Pass an optional "query" substring to find the canonical slug for a product before calling the other too…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
